newsitem.title: USA: Ford cuts loan rates on cars, sport utilities.
newsitem.headline: Ford cuts loan rates on cars, sport utilities.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. said Friday it slashed financing rates on its best-selling U.S. car models to 1.9 percent and is offering the first-ever cut-rate loans on its Ford Explorer and Mercury Mountaineer sport utility vehicles.

The 1.9-percent interest rates are being offered by Ford Motor Credit Co. on 48-month loans on the Ford Taurus, Escort, Contour and Thunderbird and the Mercury Sable, Tracer, Mystique and Cougar. They are are available through July 7, Ford said.
Previously, Ford Credit offered 7.9 percent loans on Contour and Mystique, and 4.8 percent loans on the other cars.
Cash incentives of $500 to $1,000 on the cars, offered in lieu of the cheaper financing, remain unchanged.
The moves come amid a decline in Ford's passenger car sales this year. Ford's 1997 passenger car sales through April were down 9.6 percent vs. year ago to 518,837 units.

Ford said even though it has toppled General Motors Corp. from its position as the top seller of sport utility vehicles in the United States, it is offering the first-ever retail financing incentives on its Explorer and Mountaineer.
The Ford Credit financing rates of 4.8 percent on 48-month loans on the vehicles and 5.9 percent on 49-60 month loans, are available from May 8 through June 2.
Previously, Ford had offered only leasing incentives on the compact sport utility vehicles, and consumers could only get the market interest rate.

But the vehicles have come under pressure from new sport utility entries and will face stiff competition from Chrysler Corp.'s new mid-size Dodge Durango vehicle, which will debut in the fall. Combined Explorer and Mountaineer sales for the first four months of 1997 are down 4.5 percent from a year earlier to 132,792 units.

Ford said through the first four months of 1997, its three sport utility models, which also include the new full-size Expedition, have outsold GM's eight models 200,400 units to 199,669. A year ago, GM sold 209,210 sport utility vehicles compared with Ford's to 154,412.
Ford's stock edged up 50 cents to $36.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
